Metal Gear games are different from most other military games in that your goal is to outwit and sneak past the enemy rather than engage them in open conflict. It is about using your mind, not your aggression, to achieve your goals. And I think that is the problem here (this is not an insult; it is just that if you approach the game as a straightforward shooter you are missing what this game is really all about).

if you approach the game as a straightforward shooter you are missing what this game is really all about).

Which is what, exactly? It's an open-world shooter that has some sneaking elements and dumb-as-bricks NPCs. Why give 5 LMGs when sneaking is what the game is all about? I can take out an entire base with just decoy frizbees and magazines, but that doesn't change the fact that the vast majority of weapons in the game are lethal and designed to wipe out platoons.

Which is what, exactly?

The point of the game is to achieve your objectives while avoiding conflict. Not only to avoid conflict, a truly skilled player will never even be seen (believe it or not, decoys and magazines are useful here and there but they attract the enemies attention and that actually is less than ideal...a truly expert player will plan his way around conflicts and move in and out of conflict zones like a ghost where the enemies never even notice that there is anything wrong by using cover and timing your movement around holes in patrol routes).

Sure, they give bad players lots of weapons so that they can fight off the large hordes of enemies off, but really this is a crutch. The true challenge is to find a way to complete your objectives without using any weapons. The greatest rush you can have in this game is to move in and out of a heavily guarded base and complete your mission all while completely avoiding a heavily armed enemy that can spot you at any second. There is a rush about the threat of being seen as you sneak around, and a huge sense of achievement when you are able to avoid being spotted successfully. Metal Gear has always been about this, all the way back to the game on the NES. And this emphasis on avoiding conflict rather than directly engaging is exactly what made this series so famous.

Which, more or less, may be a point that Kojima is making. It's war. It's killing people and blowing stuff up under whatever flag / nationality / religion - whatever flag you fly under, whatever reasoning you have behind it (b-b-but this a rescue mission) it's still war. It's not good, it's war.

So. Fight the good fight and try not to hurt anyone too badly to make your point, to win your war, or fight the war like it's supposed to be fought - by not being super nice and good-hearted in your attempts to, well, win your war.

If you pick the road that the game deems "good" and avoid all the unnecessary killing and explosions, you'll have an outcome that you desire, more or less, with a downside. In this case, you'd be getting your version of Snake non-Demonized, you'll have loyal followers, you'll have good ranks on all your missions, and (if you're anything like me) you'll be bored out of your mind.

Wander down yonder that second road, and you get messy. You get messy, but things are much easier fought - you still get your followers but under different pretenses. You're using the weapons of war to wage war and kill people - hardly a "good" or "noble" venture, but then ... that's war.

Just my take on it, that's all.
